events.channels: Single-source RF chip dependency for mobile-handset makers (Ericsson, Nokia)
events.name_en: Philips Albuquerque RF chip plant fire (2000)
events.name_ru: Пожар на заводе Philips в Альбукерке (2000)
events.notes: NOT WIRED - data-quality gap, not a graph-coverage gap (NLD:semiconductors, DEU:electronics, USA:electronics are all valid GEDS nodes). (1) The only sourced magnitude (50% of pre-fire capacity) is measured at the 6-month/26-week mark - a residual still-impaired level, not the peak; the actual peak (full closure) lasted the first ~3 weeks and implies a much larger trough that the research did not separately quantify. (2) No global/industry-wide pct figure exists (contrast renesas-naka-fire-2021's IHS-sourced 1.6% of global auto production) - only company-specific absolutes ($400M Ericsson sales loss, 7M handsets) - so HISTORICAL_EVENTS' required observed.auto_production_loss_pct cannot be populated without fabricating a global ratio. (3) Ericsson is Swedish; Sweden has no GEDS node, so DEU:electronics was floated as an 'approximate' downstream proxy - this is a country misattribution, not an approximation, and must not be written into cascade_spatial.csv as a DEU event. (4) The proposed USA:electronics downstream effect actually describes Nokia avoiding loss via resupply (a non-cascade resilience result), not an output_loss - labeling it as such would invert the finding. Park pending either a sourced global handset/electronics industry-wide loss pct, or an explicit decision to calibrate only the node-level NLD:semiconductors magnitude from the two-point (peak~1.0 at week 0-3, ~0.50 at week 26) shape.
events.shock_mechanism: Fire at Philips Albuquerque RF-chip fab forced ~3-week total shutdown; line still at only ~50% of pre-fire capacity 6 months later
sources: Ericsson President Kurt Hellstrom, CNNfn interview, 2000-07-21
Almar Latour 'Trial by Fire', Wall Street Journal, 2001-01-29
CNNfn 'Ericsson pulls plug on handset manufacturing', 2001-01-26

events.channels: Single-program delivery halt cascading to Boeing's airframe supply base (Spirit AeroSystems)
events.notes: NOT WIRED - graph-structure + Track-A gap. Unlike Philips, the PRIMARY node mapping is correct (USA:aerospace; Boeing is American) and the downstream cascade is correctly directional (Spirit AeroSystems output loss, not inverted). Blocked by a more fundamental limit: (1) GRAPH CANNOT REPRESENT THE OFFSET - the 737 MAX grounding's GLOBAL aerospace impact stayed small precisely because Airbus (FRA, no graph node) ramped A320neo to absorb the demand. The graph holds only USA:aerospace (89.0% of in-graph aerospace GDP) and DEU:aerospace (11.0%); with no France/Airbus node it structurally overstates global aerospace loss and has no sourced figure to validate against. (2) NO TRACK A - no tier-1 body (FAA/IATA/ICAO/AIA) published a global aerospace output-loss %; the best available (Aviation Week Airbus+Boeing deliveries -27%) is a two-firm duopoly number, not industry-body-sourced, and overstates the broad aerospace industry (defense/space/engines/MRO unaffected). (3) MAGNITUDE CONFLATION - proposed peak_magnitude 1.0 on USA:aerospace describes the 737 MAX PROGRAM (100% delivery halt), not the node: Boeing kept building 787/777/defense and other US primes (Lockheed, Northrop, GE Aviation) were largely untouched. Even the research's own Track B 0.53 is Boeing-commercial-deliveries YoY, a sub-component of the node. (4) DEU:aerospace downstream is a flagged proxy standing in for French Safran (no France node). POSITIVES recorded for future use: first regulatory-cliff (step, weeks_to_peak=0) event; CALIBRATION_GRADE node sourcing (Boeing official deliveries 806->380 = -52.9% [DERIVED]); would be the first aerospace calibration anchor (aerospace is currently uncalibrated). Unblock path: a tier-1 global aerospace output figure AND a France/Airbus node to model the duopoly offset, OR an explicit decision to calibrate node-level-only with a corrected (sub-1.0) USA:aerospace magnitude reflecting Boeing-commercial's share of the node.
events.shock_mechanism: FAA emergency airworthiness directive (Mar 13 2019) grounded the 737 MAX worldwide; Boeing cut output 52->42/month, then fully suspended MAX production Jan-May 2020; deliveries resumed after FAA rescission Nov 18 2020
sources: Boeing official delivery data via Argus Media 2020-01-13 (806 in 2018 -> 380 in 2019)
Boeing Investor Relations production-suspension press release 2019-12-16
Supply Chain Dive 2020-06-24 citing Spirit AeroSystems SEC filing

Once the raw PortWatch series was obtained and checked, the worst week of the August 2022 PLA exercises shows only -5.6% against the April-June baseline (1593 vs 1687 transits/week); the 22% figure does not appear in the data and is not reproducible. The episode also falls below the detector's 15% threshold, i.e. it is not distinguishable from ordinary weekly variation. events.name_ru: Спад полупроводникового производства Китая (экспортный контроль США + спад спроса, 2022)
events.notes: CANDIDATE, NOT WIREABLE AS-IS (2026-07 audit). A measured source-side output decline DOES exist (China NBS -11.6% YoY, rare for a semiconductor node, unlike TWN where output grew) at the untapped GOOD-tier node CHN:semiconductors. BUT it is a DEMAND-driven contraction (chip glut, not shortage) — the OPPOSITE causal direction to the engine's supply-cascade model (same structural class as the GFC demand collapse), so wiring it as a supply shock would misrepresent the physics. Attribution is also mixed (export controls + zero-COVID + demand + Ukraine). Needs a demand-side mechanism (future work) before it can be added to the calibration set.

sources: China NBS: national IC output -11.6% YoY 2022 (peak -26.7% Oct 2022, largest monthly decline since 1997)

events.channels: shipping transit; energy
events.notes: MEASURED BUT NOT YET WIREABLE (2026-08). By transit deficit this is the largest chokepoint disruption in the whole PortWatch record — deeper than the Ever Given (0.96 for days) and far longer, and deeper than the Red Sea crisis (0.48). The magnitude is measured directly from the primary series, and the node CP:Hormuz exists in the graph. The blocker is the observed TARGET: the event began 2026-03-02 and is still running at the data cutoff (2026-07-26), so no statistical agency has yet published the downstream industry output loss the benchmark calibrates against, and recovery duration is undefined for an unfinished event. Checked against the alternative explanation: PortWatch revised the Hormuz boundary in March 2026, but a definitional change produces a level shift to a new stable level, whereas the series shows a one-week 95% collapse followed by volatile partial recovery, matching the documented closure timeline to the week. Wire in once industry statistics for 2026 are published.
events.shock_mechanism: military closure of the strait to shipping
sources: IMF PortWatch daily chokepoint transits (raw series, in repo): weekly transits collapse 561 -> 25 in the week of 2026-03-08 and stay at 14-107/wk through June against a ~500-600/wk baseline
peak weekly deficit 95.5%. IRGC statement 2026-03-02 closing the strait to 'unfriendly nations'
IMO 2026-04-21: ~2,000 ships and ~20,000 mariners stranded in the Persian Gulf
